name: WM (Waste Management, Inc.)

corporate_actions.event: Completed acquisition of Stericycle (medical waste) - now 'WM Healthcare Solutions' segment
CEO Jim Fish to retire; President John Morris named CEO effective 2027-01-04

geography.fx_notes: Overwhelmingly US with Canadian operations; Stericycle added small international (Europe/LatAm) exposure. Exact split not collected in this pass (10-K segment note) - INFERENCE: US >85%.

kpis.name: Q3-26 C&D volume (reported / workday-adj.)
kpis.value: -0.4% / -0.5% (release text); internal-growth table shows C&D volume +$53m (+0.8%) - inconsistency in summary, check release

kpis.name: Capex intensity 2026E
kpis.value: ~10.4% of revenue (~$2.75bn / ~$26.4bn); ~9.5% excl. sustainability growth capex

company_fcf.definition: Operating cash flow less capex plus proceeds from divestitures

acquisitions.notes: Stericycle ~ $7.2bn EV incl. debt (closed Nov-2024) - figure from prior knowledge, not re-verified in this pass
Acquisitions contributed $33m (0.6%) to Q3 revenue growth

management.senior_turnover_5y: Planned CEO succession announced Aug-2026 (Fish -> Morris, President since May-2025); other C-suite changes not catalogued
management.succession_notes: Orderly internal succession; Morris >30 years industry experience
management.guidance_record: 2026 guidance affirmed at Q3 with revenue/FCF at high end; Q3 adj. EPS slightly below consensus ($2.15 vs $2.18 Zacks)

evidence: Collection & disposal under municipal franchises/subscriptions; non-discretionary demand (S1)
C&D yield +3.4% with volume ~flat in Q3-26 (S1)
A.rationale: Essential, recurring route-based and disposal revenue with high retention; small cyclical C&D/special waste component.

evidence: 257 active landfills; permits very hard to obtain (S3)
Morningstar wide moat for WM/RSG/WCN (MS1)
Core price 5.8% vs volume ~0% shows pricing power (S1)
B.rationale: Vertically integrated landfill network is a regulated scarce asset with demonstrated pricing power.

evidence: Adj. EBITDA margin ~31% in line with RSG, below WCN 34% (S1)
Largest landfill network in US (S3)
C.rationale: Scale delivers margins in line with top peers but not superior to WCN's secondary-market model.

evidence: Organic growth ~5% driven by price; volumes flat (S1)
RNG/recycling growth capex ($191m YTD) with commodity-linked returns (S1)
D.rationale: Mature market; growth from price, tuck-ins and sustainability projects of variable return.

evidence: Overwhelmingly US revenue (S1, INFERENCE)
E.rationale: Single-country (>70% US) concentration per anchor; developed market so risk is diversification not EM.

evidence: Planned internal CEO succession (S2)
Guidance affirmed, FCF high end (S1)
F.rationale: Long-tenured management with orderly succession; minor EPS misses.

evidence: ~90% of YTD FCF returned; $2bn buybacks 2026 (S1)
Stericycle a large diversifying deal; margin improving but integration charges continue (S1)
G.rationale: Sensible returns policy; Stericycle return on capital not yet proven.

evidence: Widely held, single share class (INFERENCE)
H.rationale: Standard large-cap US governance; pay not reviewed.

evidence: Physical collection/disposal (S1)
I1.rationale: Physical, permitted service not substitutable by AI.

evidence: No disclosed DC dependence; C&D/special waste only partly linked to construction (INFERENCE)
Route optimisation, automated MRFs and customer service automation cited by industry (INFERENCE)
Price-led contracts, landfill pricing power (S1)
I4.rationale: Strong position likely retains most savings; some municipal CPI-indexed contracts.

evidence: Energy surcharges/mandated fees recovered ($112m Q3) (S1)
Recycling/RIN prices create volatility (S1)
J.rationale: Fuel pass-through and low cyclicality; commodity/RNG exposure partial.

evidence: Adjustments for Stericycle integration ($30m Q3) and $18m landfill impairment (S1)
K.rationale: Mostly clean; recurring integration adjustments to monitor.

ai.notes: Not disclosed; INFERENCE <2% of revenue (some special-waste/C&D from DC construction).

sector_specific.env_liabilities: Landfill final capping, closure/post-closure and remediation obligations (multi-$bn; 10-K note not re-read in this pass). PFAS: leachate treatment/regulatory cost risk at landfills - quantum not disclosed.
sector_specific.commodity_sensitivity: Recycled commodities (~$82/t single stream Q3-26), RNG/RIN prices ($2.32), electricity; energy surcharge offsets fuel. Sustainability growth capex sized on these prices.

gates.notes: G1: provider ND/EBITDA 2.98x < 4.0x waste threshold; EBIT/interest comfortable (TTM EBIT $4.8bn). G4: FCF ~ net income (9M FCF $3.0bn vs TTM NI $3.1bn) - pass. G6: CEO change is not a transaction.

bull_points: Largest US landfill network (257) gives durable pricing power: core price 5.8% in Q3-26 with flat volumes.
FCF inflecting: 9M-26 FCF +42% to $3.0bn as RNG/recycling growth capex rolls off; ~90% returned to shareholders.
Stericycle margin repair (22.4% vs 17.5%) offers self-help upside.
bear_points: Volumes flat/negative: growth is almost entirely price - risk of customer/political pushback if inflation falls.
Healthcare Solutions (Stericycle) dilutes returns and carries integration charges; acquired at a premium multiple.
Sustainability investments (RNG, recycling) expose returns to RIN and commodity prices outside management control.
thesis_breakers: C&D core price falls below 4% for 2+ consecutive quarters while volume stays negative.
FCF/adj. EBITDA conversion falls back below 40% for FY2027.
Healthcare Solutions adj. EBITDA margin fails to exceed 22% by FY2027.
